the K- yield is reduced in heavy ion collisions at 1 A-GeV and at 2 A-GeV as compared to lighter systems.
the K+ and K- production in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at 1 A GeV and 1.7 A GeV is not fully understood yet.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of K-messons in heavy ion collisions at 1 AGeV is still not understood.
the K- meson yield in C+Au collisions is reduced as compared to C + C collisions at the same beam energy and that the K-/K+- ratio is underestimated by transport model calculations.
the K-/K+- ratio is sensitive to the in-medium properties of kaons and antikatons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of K-mesos in heavy-ion collisions is very sensitive to the nuclear medium.
the production of charged kaons and antiparticles in heavy ion collisions at low energy can be described by transport models only if in-medium modifications are taken into account.
the production of charged kaons and antipartons in heavy ion collisions can be used to probe in-medium modifications of the K mesons.
